title: C. Different Differences
statement:
An array a consisting of k integers is strictly increasing if a_1 < a_2 < … < a_k. For example, the arrays [1, 3, 5], [1, 2, 3, 4], [3, 5, 6] are strictly increasing; the arrays [2, 2], [3, 7, 5], [7, 4, 3], [1, 2, 2, 3] are not.

For a strictly increasing array a of k elements, let's denote the characteristic as the number of different elements in the array [a_2 - a_1, a_3 - a_2, …, a_k - a_{k-1}]. For example, the characteristic of the array [1, 3, 4, 7, 8] is 3 since the array [2, 1, 3, 1] contains 3 different elements: 2, 1 and 3.

You are given two integers k and n (k ≤ n). Construct an increasing array of k integers from 1 to n with maximum possible characteristic.

The first line contains one integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 819) — the number of test cases.

Each test case consists of one line containing two integers k and n (2 ≤ k ≤ n ≤ 40).

For each test case, print k integers — the elements of the strictly increasing array a with the maximum possible characteristic. If there are multiple answers, print any of them.

Input:
```
75 94 123 33 44 44 68 11
```

Output:
```
1 3 4 7 8
2 4 7 12
1 2 3
1 3 4
1 2 3 4
2 4 5 6
1 2 3 5 6 7 8 11
```
